Electric current is measured in amperes because the ampere is the SI base unit that quantifies the rate of flow of electric charge—one ampere equals one coulomb of charge passing a point per second (now realized via the fixed value of the elementary charge); see authoritative sources such as the BIPM SI Brochure (2019) and NIST's ampere definition for verification.
